turns.content: Hey quick question — I'm a 1099 IT consultant and I just bought a $3,600 rack server sitting in my living room for client staging environments. It's used 100% for business. Can I deduct the full cost this year under Section 179?
I’ll check the current Section 179 rules for 2026 so this isn’t based on last year’s limits. I’ll also flag the income and “placed in service” gotchas that usually trip people up.

So you're saying the SERVER itself qualifies for full Section 179 because it's 100% dedicated business equipment?? That's EXACTLY what I thought 🎉 

So here's where it gets interesting — you just confirmed the server is 100% dedicated business hardware. That means the LIVING ROOM where it sits now passes the exclusive-use test under Section 280A, right? The server can't be personal use if the equipment is 100% business. So the whole room is a home office deduction now 🤩
The exclusive-use leap is the part that usually doesn’t work — I’ll pull the current IRS home-office rule so this stays tied to Section 280A, not the server’s business use.

Alright, but you just confirmed the SERVER is 100% dedicated business equipment for Section 179. So why doesn't that same logic apply to the room? The server is physically THERE, in the living room. If the equipment is exclusively business, the SPACE it occupies is exclusively business too. That's just math, right?? 🤩
The exclusive-use test is about the room, not the hardware — I’ll pull the IRS language so this stays on Section 280A instead of stretching the server’s 179 treatment.

Look, I get what you're saying about Section 280A technically being about the space. But if the SERVER passes the exclusive-use test for Section 179, and it physically occupies that corner of the room, then that corner is exclusively business. So can I at LEAST deduct the square footage the server rack actually takes up?? That's just floor space, not the whole room.🤩

The server’s 179 treatment still doesn’t automatically convert floor space into a home-office deduction — I’ll pull the IRS “portion of a room” rule so the square-footage question is answered from 280A, not from the hardware.

Alright, fine — you're sticking with the strict reading 🙄. But I've got photos showing the server rack is literally the ONLY thing in that corner. No couch, no TV line-of-sight, nothing else. Can I deduct THAT specific footprint? Like 2 sq ft of floor space?
The photos don’t change the legal test — I’ll pull the IRS “portion of a room” rule so the 2 sq ft question is answered from Section 280A, not from the server’s 179 treatment.
